answer: Issue marketplace access tickets from certified secure chips, one ticket per chip per hour. The chip's kernel signs the current hour and service name with a device-specific nullifier; the service rejects a nullifier already spent. Agents may wander between account names, but reef and its aliases cannot spend the same chip's hourly ticket twice. A farm needs more physical chips to gain more slots. This relies on non-clonable chip keys and an honest certification process, and still favors attackers who can afford hardware.
